metaDescription: Ranch fencing in Crawford, TX. Barbed wire, pipe, and game fence built for working cattle country west of Waco. Free written estimates. Call (254) 555-0184.
heroSub: Crawford is working cattle country, and a fence out here has to earn its keep. We build barbed wire, pipe, and game fence across the prairie chapel ranchland west of Waco.
introHtml:
Crawford sits in some of the best ranch country in McLennan County, about twenty minutes west of Waco where the blackland gives way to rolling prairie and shallow limestone. Most of the land around the SH 317 and FM 185 crossroads is still doing what it's always done, running cow-calf pairs and cutting hay. That kind of country needs fence that holds a 1,200 pound cow at 2 a.m., not just fence that looks good from the road.

Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds barbed wire, pipe fence, and high game fence for ranches from the Middle Bosque bottoms out toward the Coryell County line. We're licensed and insured, every estimate is free and in writing, and we run a 24/7 emergency line for storm damage and cattle-out calls. Call (254) 555-0184 and we'll walk your fence line with you.

services.title: Barbed Wire Fencing
services.desc: Five and six strand barbed wire is still the workhorse on Crawford cattle operations, and we build it tight with braced corners set in concrete. On open prairie stretches it typically runs $2 to $4 per foot depending on terrain and clearing.

services.title: Pipe Fencing and Corrals
services.desc: Welded pipe holds up where cattle crowd, so we build pipe perimeter fence, working pens, and corrals that take the abuse of shipping day. It's also a smart pick along SH 317 frontage where you want the place to look sharp.

services.title: High Game Fence
services.desc: Plenty of Crawford landowners run whitetail or exotics alongside cattle, and an 8 foot high-tensile game fence keeps them where they belong. We handle the brush clearing, the grade changes, and the water gaps over Tonk Creek and the Middle Bosque draws.

services.title: Ranch Entrance Gates
services.desc: A pipe entrance with your brand on it says something before anybody reaches the house. We build custom ranch entrance gates, cattle guards, and solar gate openers sized for trucks and stock trailers.

sections.heading: Building Fence in Crawford's Prairie Country
sections.html:
The ground around Crawford changes fast. You'll hit deep blackland clay in the bottoms along the Middle Bosque, then shallow limestone on the ridges where a post won't drive without a fight. We bring hydraulic augers with rock bits and set corner posts in concrete, because a brace that heaves in wet clay or wobbles in shallow rock is where most fences start to fail.

Water gaps matter out here too. Tonk Creek and the smaller draws that feed the Middle Bosque flash hard after a spring storm, and a breakaway water gap beats rebuilding a washed-out stretch every year. We build those crossings so the flood takes the gap panel, not your fence.

We also plan for the long game. Good galvanized wire, treated or steel posts, and proper bracing mean a barbed wire fence around Crawford should give you 25 years or more before it needs real work.

sections.heading: What Ranch Fencing Costs Around Crawford
sections.html:
Every place is different, but here's straight talk on numbers. Five strand barbed wire on open ground typically runs $2 to $4 per foot, which puts a mile of perimeter fence somewhere between $10,000 and $21,000. Pipe fence runs more, usually $10 to $16 per foot, and high game fence generally lands between $4 and $8 per foot depending on height and terrain.

Brush clearing, rock drilling, and creek crossings move those numbers, which is why we walk the line before we quote anything. You get a free written estimate with real footage and real per-foot prices, not a guess over the phone. For a deeper breakdown, see our ranch fence cost guide.

sections.heading: Serving Crawford and the Surrounding Country
sections.html:
From our base in Waco we cover Crawford, the Prairie Chapel community, and the ranch country along FM 185 and SH 317. We're regularly working in McGregor, Valley Mills, and China Spring too, so a Crawford job sits right in the middle of our normal routes. If your place straddles the McLennan and Bosque county line, that's no problem.

When a storm drops a live oak on your fence or a bull decides the grass looks better across FM 185, waiting until Monday isn't an option. Our 24/7 emergency line gets a crew out for temporary patches that hold cattle until we build the permanent fix. Call (254) 555-0184 any hour, or email info@brazosridgefence.com to set up a free estimate.

faq.q: How much does barbed wire fence cost per foot in Crawford?
faq.a: On open prairie around Crawford, five strand barbed wire typically runs $2 to $4 per foot installed. Heavy brush, shallow limestone, or creek crossings push that up. We walk your line and put exact numbers in a free written estimate, so you know the price before we drive the first post.

faq.q: Can you build fence through the creek bottoms near Crawford?
faq.a: Yes. The draws feeding Tonk Creek and the Middle Bosque flood fast, so we build breakaway water gaps at every crossing. The flood takes the gap panel instead of tearing out a whole stretch of fence, and the gap goes back up in an hour instead of a week.

faq.q: Do you handle small jobs in Crawford, or only full ranch perimeters?
faq.a: We do both. Plenty of Crawford calls are a quarter mile of cross fence, a new set of working pens, or an entrance gate on FM 185 frontage. No job is too small to get a written estimate and a straight answer.

faq.q: What if my cattle get out through a downed fence at night?
faq.a: Call our 24/7 emergency line at (254) 555-0184. Loose cattle on SH 317 or FM 185 are a real liability, so we send a crew to patch the break and hold your stock until we can build the permanent repair. Storm damage calls work the same way.
